A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eIF4E is not only a key host factor for PVY infection, but also a key regulator of host defense response against viral infection.
eIF4E has a dual role in the host: it is a host dependency factor for PVY and also a regulator of the host defense.
eIF4E is a multifunctional protein, and its overexpression can trigger multiple layers of antiviral defense, which is beneficial for the development of PVY resistance in potato.
The main takeaway from our work is that

eIF4E may not be a simple, passive host dependency factor, but instead may actively participate in the host response to infection, potentially by acting as an upstream regulator of a broader host defense response.
over-expression of eIF4E in potato results in the suppression of the wild-type eIF4E transcript, which may explain the high level of resistance to PVY observed in these plants.
